properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 31 at 3:32PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 331 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 13 miles north of Boone to near Pueblo Depot to
8 miles northwest of Pueblo West. Movement was southeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, pea size hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Pueblo, Pueblo Airport, Fountain, Fowler, Olney Springs, Boone,
Pueblo Reservoir, Salt Creek, Pueblo Depot, Pinon, Blende, Pueblo
West, Avondale, and Hanover.
properties.areaDesc: Colorado Springs Vicinity/Southern El Paso County/Rampart Range Below 7400 Ft; Pueblo Vicinity/Pueblo County Below 6300 Feet; Crowley County; La Junta Vicinity/Otero County

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 31 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 314 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
La Veta Pass, or 38 miles east of Alamosa, moving southeast at 15
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, half inch hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Ponding of water on paved roadways, and washouts
of dirt roads will be possible.  Creeks, streams and dry
washes may experience rapid rises.

Locations impacted include...
La Veta, La Veta Pass, Spring Burn Scar south of Highway 160 in
Costilla county, Spring Burn Scar north of Highway 160, Indian Creek
on the southeastern Spring Burn Scar, and Spring Burn Scar south of
Highway 160 in Huerfano county.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 3:06PM MDT until July 31 at 5:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 306 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Peyton and Ellicott.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Black Squirrel Creek and its tributaries.
